levels.title: Two halves
levels.goal: Build a graph with one input and one output, wired through server.
levels.body:
A Shiny app has two halves.
UI declares widgets and placeholders. Server fills those placeholders from data.
Nothing is magic: every output is computed from inputs and reactives.
levels.hint: Add an input node named x, an output node named out, then connect them.
levels.solution:
node input x
node output out
edge x out

levels.title: The reactive pipe
levels.goal: Insert a reactive between input and output.
levels.body:
Outputs should stay thin. Put shared math in a reactive expression.
It recomputes only when its dependencies change, then feeds every consumer.
levels.hint: node reactive y — then edge x→y and y→out.
levels.solution:
edge-del x out
node reactive y
edge x y
edge y out

levels.title: One reactive, many consumers
levels.goal: Fan one reactive into two outputs without duplicating the math.
levels.body:
When two outputs need the same value, do not copy the formula.
One reactive, two edges out. Invalidation stays automatic.
levels.hint: Keep y. Add out2 and edge y→out2.
levels.solution:
node output out2
edge y out2

levels.title: Observers are not the data path
levels.goal: Add an observer that watches x but does not feed an output.
levels.body:
Observers run for side effects: logs, writes, notifications.
They are not cached values. Never wire an observer as the source of an output.
levels.hint: node observer log — edge x→log only. No edge into out from log.
levels.solution:
node observer log
edge x log

levels.title: Break a dependency with isolate
levels.goal: Keep x→out, but read a value from n without taking a dependency on n.
levels.body:
reactive.value n feeds observer clear.
If out also reads n, out would re-run every time n changes.
Use isolate so out only re-runs when x changes.
levels.hint: Edge n→clear and n→iso, but do NOT edge n→out. iso is a reactive marked as isolated read.
levels.solution:
node reactive iso
edge n iso
edge iso out
